chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Abdullah ibn Usman, from a man, from Minhal, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and upon me was a sleek sandal, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'This is a shoe (footwear) of the Jews'. So Minhal went and took a knife, so he (made a) curve in the middle with it.

key_terms.فَخَصَّرَهَا: He curved it or made a hollow/curve in the middle (of the sandal).
key_terms.مَمْسُوحَةٌ: Smoothed, sleek, or uncarved; referring to the surface of the sandal lacking distinct carving or texture.
key_terms.نَعْلٌ: Sandal or shoe, typically referring to simple leather footwear.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the style of footwear (sleek vs. carved) in Shia jurisprudence based on this hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) identifies Minhal’s smooth-soled sandal as the distinctive style of the Jews, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential concept of *tashabbuh* (imitation of non-Muslims). Minhal’s immediate action of carving the sole with a knife demonstrates the practical application of this ruling, where altering the physical form serves to distinguish Muslims from other religious communities in daily attire.
